title: Learning Hierarchical Patch Splitting Policies for Faster Vision Transformers
abstract: arXiv:2611.05742v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) are bottlenecked by the length of their input token sequence. Standard patchification fixes this length with a single patch size applied across the image, regardless of regional content. Prior work on adaptive patch sizing reduces token count by assigning coarser patches to visually simple regions, but relies on noisy pixel-level heuristics such as local entropy to make patchification decisions. We argue that this compute allocation should be grounded in the model's interpretation of task relevant information, not in raw pixel statistics. We introduce Split Policy Learned Image Tokenization which learns to allocate token resolution based on what the model finds meaningful, producing shorter token sequences that are better matched to task-relevant content. SPLIT matches the accuracy of full-resolution ViT classification baselines while using 30% fewer tokens. The same gains hold on dense prediction: SPLIT achi

translated_title: 学习分层图像块切分策略以加速视觉Transformer
translated_abstract: 视觉Transformer（ViT）的性能瓶颈在于其输入token序列的长度。标准的图像块化通过在整个图像上应用统一的patch大小来固定该长度，而不考虑各区域的内容。以往关于自适应patch大小的工作通过为视觉上简单的区域分配更粗糙的patch来减少token数量，但这类方法依赖于局部熵等含噪声的像素级启发式方法来做出patch化决策。我们认为，这种计算资源的分配应该基于模型对任务相关信息的理解，而不是原始的像素统计。我们提出了SPLIT（Split Policy Learned Image Tokenization，学习切分策略的图像token化方法），它学习根据模型认为有意义的内容来分配token分辨率，从而产生与任务相关内容更好匹配的更短token序列。SPLIT在使用减少30%的token的情况下，达到了全分辨率ViT分类基线的准确率。同样的收益也体现在密集预测任务上。（注：原始摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出SPLIT方法，通过学习依据模型认为有意义的任务相关内容来分配图像token分辨率，替代基于像素统计的启发式方法，在减少30%token数量的同时保持与全分辨率ViT相当的准确率。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes SPLIT, a learned image tokenization approach that allocates token resolution based on the model's interpretation of task-relevant information rather than noisy pixel-level heuristics, matching full-resolution ViT accuracy while using 30% fewer tokens.
